articles.title: Disclosure Day’s first trailer teases close encounters of a different kind
articles.summary: Steven Spielberg’s Disclosure Day — in theaters June 12th, 2026 — teases alien contact in new trailer.
articles.body: The first trailer for Steven Spielberg’s upcoming film Disclosure Day is here, and it will leave you with more questions than answers about what exactly is going on. There is no denying that something strange is happening to a Kansas City newscaster (Emily Blunt) who goes into a strange trance on-air in Disclosure Day’s new trailer. The odd clicks coming out of her mouth sound inhuman and leave everyone watching alarmed because it seems like she might be having a fit. But the woman seems much more…together in the presence of a mysterious man (Josh O’Connor) who says he knows the truth and wants to share it with everyone living on Earth. The way he appears to be able to create crop circles just by standing in a field suggests that alien shenanigans are afoot, but we won’t know for sure until the film debuts on June 12th, 2026.

articles.title: Star Fox is the Switch 2’s most impressive visual showcase yet
articles.summary: Nintendo’s latest remake retains the classic N64 shooter action, but with a cinematic makeover.
articles.body: The biggest Switch 2 exclusives so far have largely been about scale. Mario Kart World introduced a wide open continent to race across, Donkey Kong Bananza let you smash basically everything around you, and Pokopia brought an expansive Minecraft-style creative experience to the Pokémon universe. Star Fox is different. A remake of a Nintendo 64 game, Star Fox is an on-rails shooter, with tightly choreographed action and spectacular set-pieces. This more linear structure has let the game’s designers craft what is perhaps the best-looking game yet for the Switch 2. Considering that Star Fox is at its best when it makes you feel like you’re right in the middle of a gorgeous sci-fi movie, those visual flourishes make a big difference. Star Fox follows the same basic blueprint of the game it’s based on, Star Fox 64. The game has you taking control of an anthropomorphic fox pilot named Fox McCloud (fresh off a surprise appearance in The Super Mario Galaxy Movie), who leads a squadron of mercenaries that fight for good, but also money. The story is pretty barebones, but it has Fox and friends taking on a series of missions across the galaxy in an attempt to defeat an evil scientist named Andross. The general storyline, the overall structure of the game, and even the layout of the levels remain largely unchanged from the N64 version. But even if you’ve played the original, the differences between the two are apparent right away. Star Fox’s missions are all accompanied by voiced cutscenes that flesh out the story and give you better reasons for why you’re heading out on a particular mission. They also let you spend a lot more time with the characters outside of their ships. I never knew I wanted to see Fox sipping an energy drink in between battles, but it turns out I do. This all makes the game feel more cinematic, much like a modern action game, and the feeling extends seamlessly into the action itself. It simply looks incredible: ships flying across an ocean, leaving trails in the water; gigantic enemies that take up the whole screen, while waves of lava crash down around them; and all kinds of firefights amidst huge swaths of debris floating in space. If you take out the talking animals and delightfully cheesy dialogue, you could mistake the game for other space epics like Star Wars or No Man’s Sky. The visuals and cutscenes go a long way to making the nearly three decade-old Star Fox 64 look and feel modern. So do the controls, which seem much more responsive to me (though maybe that’s just because I’m not being forced to use an N64 controller this time around). For an example of how different the game can look, here’s a glimpse at one of its most iconic scenes from early on, compared across the Switch 2 and the N64 version available through a Switch Online subscription. [Image: [Image: But there’s also a lot about Star Fox that shows its age. This is an old-school, arcade-style space shooter, which means that it’s a game built around repetition. The initial path through the game only takes around an hour, but to see everything it has to offer, you have to replay levels to find new paths that open up additional missions and, ultimately, the true ending. That takes a lot of time, particularly as some of the levels remain pretty difficult. I love the idea of the train mission where you pilot a tank, but after a few hours of struggling through it, I definitely don’t want to try and shoot all of the necessary targets ever again. There’s nothing necessarily wrong with this structure, and I do occasionally enjoy going back and trying for a high score. But it can also feel incongruous with the modern presentation, which suggests you’re experiencing a movie-like story. The barebones narrative feels even more lacking now given how epic the visuals make everything feel, and while the cutscenes look great, the set-up means you’ll see them many, many times. They’re impressive at first, but eventually you’ll be making liberal use of the skip button. [Media: Star Fox features a handful of other additions. A new challenge mode gives you more goals to achieve in each level; an expanded multiplayer includes online play; and there are some wacky virtual avatars that I wasn’t able to test. These are all nice to have, though the meat of the experience remains the campaign and all of its various unlockable missions. The game is launching at a time when remakes are among the most popular single-player titles out there. Major franchises like Resident Evil, Final Fantasy, and Dragon Quest have all turned remakes into tentpole releases, while some of the most anticipated upcoming games — including Halo: Campaign Evolved and Nintendo’s own mysterious Ocarina of Time remake — are updates to classic titles. Star Fox is illustrative of both the good and bad of this trend. In many ways, the visual overhaul benefits the experience, making it feel even more like a sci-fi movie you can play. But it also shows how awkward it can be when old-school gameplay meets modern graphics. In this case, the balance mostly works out in Star Fox’s favor. But it also has me more curious than ever to see how Nintendo remakes one of the most iconic and influential Zelda games. Star Fox launches on the Nintendo Switch 2 on June 25th.

articles.title: Com show de Ebony, Maceió Pop Festival reúne atrações em 9h de festa | G1
articles.standfirst: Evento acontece nesta sexta-feira (11), em Jaraguá, e reúne atrações de rap, pop e hyperpop em 9 horas de festa.
articles.summary: Evento acontece nesta sexta-feira (11), em Jaraguá, e reúne atrações de rap, pop e hyperpop em 9 horas de festa.
articles.body:
O Maceió Pop Festival chega à terceira edição nesta sexta-feira (11), com shows de Ebony, Katy da Voz e as Abusadas e Huná, além de apresentações de DJs e drag queens. O evento começa às 20h, na Fábrica de Eventos, no bairro de Jaraguá, em Maceió.

A programação terá cerca de nove horas de duração e reúne atrações nacionais e alagoanas ligadas ao rap, pop, K-pop, electropop e hyperpop.

Entre os destaques está Ebony, nome do rap feminino brasileiro. A programação também inclui Katy da Voz e as Abusadas, com repertório ligado ao pop experimental, e a cantora alagoana Huná, que apresenta composições de rap.

Segundo a organização, a edição deste ano terá estrutura e espaço ampliados em relação aos anos anteriores.

“É uma edição completamente renovada, com uma nova estrutura e uma programação pensada para celebrar tudo aquilo que faz a cultura pop ser tão diversa, exagerada, divertida e inesquecível. Esta edição promete ser a maior de todas”, afirmou o DJ e produtor do festival Gil Silva.

Os DJs Del, Brigadeiro, Gil, Gigis Banks, FJSANN e Erms também integram a programação. Os sets terão músicas de diferentes épocas e vertentes do pop, com referências a artistas como Britney Spears, Lady Gaga, Beyoncé, Ariana Grande, Katy Perry, Anitta, Marina Sena e Duda Beat.

O DJ Erms será responsável por um set especial de hyperpop.

“Cada set é montado com muito carinho e atenção a determinado tema, justamente para fazer com que o público se divirta e resgate memórias afetivas relacionadas a determinadas músicas”, disse o DJ Brigadeiro.

O festival também terá performances das drag queens alagoanas Alejandra Vortex, Aurora Blossom, Gina Kynnors, Kiki Kloss, Lalacra Nox, Lavinia Burtner, Santana Blossom, Saphira Star e Skarllet Fuck'Sia.

Os horários de cada apresentação ainda serão divulgados pela organização.

articles.title: Filme pré-selecionado para ir ao Oscar 2027 foi gravado no Ceará | G1
articles.standfirst: Filme cearense e outros cinco longas disputam a indicação brasileira para tentar concorrer ao Oscar 2027. No elenco, estão Lázaro Ramos, Teca Pereira e o menino Yuri Gomes.
articles.summary: Filme cearense e outros cinco longas disputam a indicação brasileira para tentar concorrer ao Oscar 2027. No elenco, estão Lázaro Ramos, Teca Pereira e o menino Yuri Gomes.
articles.body:
Filme cearense "Feito pipa" é pré-selecionado para representar o Brasil no Oscar — Foto: Divulgação/Paris Filmes

O filme cearense "Feito Pipa", um dos seis pré-selecionados para representar o Brasil na disputa por uma vaga na categoria de Melhor Filme Internacional do Oscar 2027 , foi gravado na cidade de Quixadá , no sertão central do Ceará. A decisão final do filme que vai representar o Brasil na maior competição do cinema mundial será anunciada no dia 16 de setembro.

"Feito Pipa" estreia nos cinemas no dia 5 de novembro. O longa-metragem conta a história de Gugu, um garoto de 11 anos apaixonado por futebol e criado pela avó, Dilma, uma professora aposentada que dá a ele liberdade e afeto. Quando a saúde dela piora devido ao mal de Alzheimer, o garoto precisa lidar com a possibilidade de ter que morar o com pai, Batista, com quem tem uma relação distante.

O ator baiano Yuri Gomes dá vida ao pequeno Gugu. A atriz Teca Pereira interpreta Dilma, a avó do garoto, e Lázaro Ramos interpreta Batista, o pai dele. A obra tem roteiro de André Araújo e direção de Allan Deberton, dois cearenses nascidos em Russas, no interior do Ceará.

Lázaro Ramos interpreta Batista, pai de Gugu, personagem do ator Yuri Gomes no filme "Feito pipa" — Foto: Divulgação/Paris Filmes

O longa ganhou cinco prêmios no Festival de Gramado , um dos mais tradicionais do Brasil, entre eles o de melhor atriz para Teca Pereira e o de Melhor Ator Coadjuvante para Lázaro Ramos. O filme também venceu o prêmio Júri Popular do Festival de Gramado, sendo eleito pelo público como seu filme favorito no evento.

O roteiro de "Feito Pipa" foi construído durante o Laboratório de Cinema da Escola Porto Iracema das Artes , em Fortaleza. Anualmente, o laboratório seleciona seis projetos e, ao longo de sete meses, os roteiristas recebem apoio financeiro e criativo, por meio de mentorias com roteiristas em atuação, para aprimorar seus roteiros.

Na corrida pelo Oscar, o longa cearense concorreu inicialmente em uma lista de 15 filmes inscritos e habilitados para a ser o representante brasileiro na premiação. Da lista, sobraram seis na pré-seleção. A decisão final da comissão será tomada em 16 de setembro. A seleção é feita pela Academia Brasileira de Cinema .

Depois de ser selecionado, a candidatura do filme brasileiro é submetida ao Oscar e concorre junto aos filmes de outros países por uma vaga nas categorias pleiteadas. O filme escolhido pelo Brasil, portanto, pode ou não ser selecionado para concorrer. Se for escolhido, o longa brasileiro irá concorrer na cerimônia do Oscar 2027, que está marcada para 14 de março de 2027.

articles.title: Kiko Dinucci cruza a selva da cidade de São Paulo entre as guitarras e ruídos experimentais do álbum solo 'Medusa'  | G1
articles.standfirst: Parcerias do artista com Maria Beraldo e Romulo Fróes sobressaem no repertório autoral do belo álbum.
articles.summary: Parcerias do artista com Maria Beraldo e Romulo Fróes sobressaem no repertório autoral do belo álbum.
articles.body:
Kiko Dinucci lança hoje, 9 de setembro, o terceiro álbum solo, 'Medusa', com repertório inteiramente autoral — Foto: Aline Belfort / Divulgação

♬ Nona música do álbum “Medusa”, na disposição das dez faixas do terceiro disco solo de estúdio de Kiko Dinucci, “Como foi?” é bela balada de coração partido composta pelo artista paulistano com Romulo Fróes. Pela redonda arquitetura melódica, a canção poderia ter vindo com a assinatura de Roberto Carlos ou de Nando Reis, que não é nenhum Roberto, mas às vezes chega tão perto que até o ultrapassa.

Contudo, na voz de Dinucci, “Como foi?” é atravessada por ruídos na metade final da gravação de quase seis minutos, em sintonia com o tom experimental do álbum “Medusa”, primeiro disco solo do artista desde “Rastilho” (2020), álbum lançado há seis anos.

No mundo a partir de hoje, quarta-feira, 9 de setembro, em edição do selo Risco, “Medusa” é álbum de guitarras, fitas e samplers em que Dinucci radicaliza na experimentação.

Cantor, compositor e guitarrista, Kiko Dinucci é um dos nomes fundamentais da cena indie paulistana do século XXI, integrando turma que inclui outros expoentes dessa cena, como Rodrigo Campos, o supracitado Romulo Fróes e Juçara Marçal, nome aliás recorrente nas dez faixas de “Medusa”, álbum produzido por Dinucci sob a direção de Juçara.

Com capa que expõe obra criada pela artista plástica Tatiana Blass com inspiração na música “Faca da palavra”, o álbum “Medusa” transita por universo fiel ao som de Kiko Dinucci. “Claudia, Frota e eu”, parceria de Dinucci com Negro Leo, pode ser rotulada como samba em esquema noise que evoca a atmosfera de uma ou outra faixa do primeiro álbum individual do artista, “Cortes curtos” (2017), trabalho de ambiência punk que abriu a discografia solo de Dinucci há nove anos.

Também seguindo a cadência do samba, mas em tom (um pouco) mais tradicional, “Segundo eterno” é tema composto por Dinucci para a trilha sonora da peça “Avenida Paulista” (2025), encenada por Felipe Hirsch. Quando Dinucci fala em “calçada, gente correndo rumo à morte” em verso desse samba, o artista está falando da cidade natal de São Paulo (SP).

Kiko Dinucci apresenta grandes parcerias com Maria Beraldo e Romulo Fróes na safra autoral do álbum 'Medusa' — Foto: Pablo Saborido / Divulgação

É na selva dessa cidade que vaga, sem destino e sem paz, o personagem-título de “Cão perdido”, música climática que abre o disco em faixa gravada por Dinucci com a colaboração do guitarrista Lello Bezerra no arranjo e na produção musical. Na ruidosa “Água viva”, parceria de Dinucci com Sophia Chablau, a colaboração é de Podeserdesligado, codinome artístico de produtora musical carioca (residente em São Paulo) ligada ao universo da música experimental.

Podeserdesligado também contribui, ao lado de Gustavo Infante, para a formatação de “Casca do olho”, samba com ecos do som industrial da banda alemã Einstürzende Neubauten. Já “Loira Palmer”, música de alto teor erótico composta e cantada por Dinucci com Crystal Duarte (da banda fluminense Vera Fisher Era Clubber), remete ao universo surrealista dos filmes do cineasta norte-americano David Lynch (1946 – 2025), falecido no ano passado.

E assim – entre angústias, gozos, ecos do Sonic Youth e ruídos – caminha a humanidade de Kiko Dinucci em “Medusa”, álbum que traz a voz de Maria Beraldo em “Cascuda”, coautora dessa música ouvida em bela gravação melancólica que rasga a cidade com o som da ferragem , como poetiza um verso da letra.

É assim, com o som da ferragem, que Kiko Dinucci cruza a selva da cidade de São Paulo (SP) – sem paz e sem destino como um cão perdido – entre as guitarras e os ruídos experimentais do álbum “Medusa”.

articles.title: 'A Fabulosa Máquina do Tempo' avança na disputa por vaga no Oscar 2027 | G1
articles.standfirst: Produção aborda temas como gênero, casamento e maternidade por meio de entrevistas conduzidas por crianças.
articles.summary: Gravada no Piauí, produção aborda temas como gênero, casamento e maternidade por meio de entrevistas conduzidas por crianças.
articles.body:
O documentário "A Fabulosa Máquina do Tempo ", gravado em Guaribas , no Sul do Piauí, entrou na lista final de filmes que disputam uma vaga para representar o Brasil na categoria de Melhor Filme Internacional do Oscar 2027. A lista foi divulgada nesta quarta-feira (9) pela Academia Brasileira de Cinema.

A produção integra uma lista com outras cinco obras brasileiras . Dirigido por Eliza Capai, o documentário propõe reflexões sobre relações de gênero, casamento e maternidade por meio de brincadeiras e entrevistas conduzidas por crianças.

"A Fabulosa Maquina do Tempo fez a incrível façanha de ser o único documentário na lista de filmes para representar o Brasil no Oscar", comemorou a diretora nas redes sociais.

O processo de seleção começou em agosto, quando foi divulgada uma lista com 15 produções inscritas . Agora, seis filmes seguem na disputa pela indicação brasileira.

O resultado da obra que representará o Brasil na corrida pelo Oscar será anunciado na próxima quarta-feira (16).

Segundo a distribuidora, instituições, coletivos e cineclubes podem solicitar exibições coletivas e gratuitas do documentário por meio de um formulário on-line .

Ao g1 , a diretora contou que as gravações ocorreram em 2021 e as crianças que participaram do filme receberam uma oficina de vídeo, na qual aprenderam técnicas de entrevista que são utilizadas para questionar as mãe e avós sobre dificuldades enfrentadas ao longo da vida, casamento e maternidade.

As respostas e a forma como as crianças interpretam essas histórias são retratadas por meio de brincadeiras e conversas.

“Eu entrevisto elas, elas entrevistam as mães e descobrem coisas muitas vezes duras. Em uma cena, a mãe conta à filha que seu maior medo é perder os filhos. Sofia, que tinha nove anos, responde que crianças não morrem e sai para brincar de zumbi”, relembrou.

articles.title: Eleições Boi Garantido 2026: Marialvo Brandão disputa presidência | G1
articles.standfirst: O candidato se notabilizou na instituição como um dos principais artistas de alegorias do Festival de Parintins
articles.summary: Candidato nas eleições Garantido 2026, o artista Marialvo Brandão apresenta seus planos para a diretoria da agremiação no próximo triênio em Parintins.
articles.body:
Os sócios do boi Garantido votam no dia 13 de setembro para escolher a nova diretoria da agremiação em Parintins , no interior do Amazonas. O pleito vai definir quem estará à frente do boi no triênio de 2027 a 2029. Marialvo Brandão concorre pela Chapa 30 que tem como lema "Por um Garantido Campeão”. O g1 pediu aos candidatos que apresentassem propostas e deixassem uma mensagem aos sócios. (Assista acima).

O candidato se notabilizou na instituição como um dos principais artistas de alegorias do Festival de Parintins. Sua trajetória no Garantido inclui passagens pelo setor administrativo, entre elas o cargo de vice-presidente, que ocupa atualmente.

No Garantido, três chapas disputam a presidência: Marialvo Brandão e Albano Albuquerque — Chapa "Por um Garantido Campeão"; Rafael Júnior e Clodoaldo Batista — Chapa Garantido Campeão; e Ronildo Monteverde e Alan Gomes — Chapa Raízes Fortes. Apenas associados têm direito a participar da eleição.

articles.title: Veja os seis filmes brasileiros pré-selecionados para o Oscar 2027 | G1
articles.standfirst: Os longas foram escolhidos entre 15 inscritos; representante brasileiro na categoria de Melhor Filme Internacional será definido em 16 de setembro.
articles.summary: Os longas foram escolhidos entre 15 inscritos; representante brasileiro na categoria de Melhor Filme Internacional será definido em 16 de setembro.
articles.body:
Montagem com os seis filmes escolhidos pela Academia Brasileira de Cinema. — Foto: Reprodução

A Academia Brasileira de Cinema anunciou nesta terça-feira (9) os seis filmes pré-selecionados para representar o Brasil na disputa por uma vaga na categoria de Melhor Filme Internacional do Oscar 2027.

Ao todo, 15 longas-metragens foram inscritos e habilitados para a seleção. Agora, a comissão responsável pela escolha vai definir qual dos seis títulos será o representante brasileiro na premiação.

A decisão final será tomada em 16 de setembro, quando a comissão fará a última reunião. A cerimônia do Oscar 2027 está marcada para 14 de março de 2027.

Veja abaixo os seis filmes que estão na disputa:

Cartaz do filme '100 Dias'. — Foto: Reprodução.

O filme, dirigido por Carlos Saldanha, acompanha o navegador Amyr Klink durante uma travessia do Atlântico Sul a remo entre a África e o Brasil. Sozinho em um pequeno barco, ele enfrenta o medo, a solidão e os limites físicos e psicológicos impostos pela jornada.

A viagem também leva o personagem a revisitar memórias, conflitos familiares e escolhas do passado. A travessia pelo oceano se transforma, assim, em uma jornada de autoconhecimento.

Cartaz do filme 'A Fabulosa Máquina do Tempo'. — Foto: Reprodução

No filme de Eliza Capai, que se passa no sertão do Piauí, meninas entre a infância e a adolescência imaginam uma máquina do tempo para revisitar as histórias de suas mães e avós. Entre cultos evangélicos, redes sociais e sonhos para o futuro, elas refletem sobre pobreza, desigualdade e o que significa se tornar mulher.

Cartaz do filme 'A Natureza das Coisas Invisíveis'. — Foto: Reprodução

De Rafaela Camelo, o longa apresenta Glória, de 10 anos, que passa as férias no hospital onde a mãe trabalha como enfermeira. É lá que ela conhece Sofia, uma menina preocupada com a saúde da bisavó e convencida de que a internação no hospital contribuiu para a piora dela.

As duas criam uma amizade a partir do desejo de deixar o hospital. Depois, elas e suas mães seguem para um refúgio no interior de Goiás, onde vivem os últimos dias de um verão marcado por descobertas e despedidas. O longa é uma coprodução entre Brasil e Chile.

Cartaz do filme 'Feito Pipa'.' — Foto: Reprodução

Gugu é um garoto de 12 anos apaixonado por futebol e criado pela avó, Dilma, uma professora aposentada que oferece a ele uma vida livre, afetiva e criativa. A relação com o pai, Batista, é diferente e marcada por ausências, expectativas e sentimentos que não são colocados em palavras. O conflito ganha força quando Gugu precisa enfrentar a possibilidade de passar a morar com o pai. O filme é de Allan Deberton.

Cartaz do filme 'Nosso Segredo' — Foto: Reprodução

O filme de Grace Passô acompanha uma família negra que tenta reconstruir a rotina depois de sofrer uma perda recente. Cada integrante lida com o luto de uma maneira diferente, enquanto o filho mais novo guarda um segredo. A revelação desse segredo faz com que a família encare as raízes de suas dores e tente encontrar, junta, um novo caminho.

Cartaz do filme 'Vicentina Pede Desculpas'. — Foto: Reprodução

Em uma manhã em Belo Horizonte, um ônibus lotado sofre um acidente depois de desviar da pista e cair em uma avenida. Um passageiro fica gravemente ferido, enquanto os demais ocupantes, incluindo o motorista Wesley, morrem.

Imagens de câmeras de segurança levantam especulações de que o motorista poderia ter provocado o acidente de propósito. A tragédia deixa Vicentina, uma professora aposentada de 75 anos e mãe de Wesley, devastada.

Sem saber como seguir em frente, ela decide procurar as famílias das vítimas para pedir desculpas. Na busca por respostas, porém, Vicentina encontra situações e verdades que nem sempre são as que esperava. O filme é de Gabriel Martins .

articles.title: Fã que cantou com Bring me the Horizon diz que estava 'preparado para ser humilhado na internet' | G1
articles.standfirst: Ao g1, João Pedro Rodrigues, de anos 24, conta que o vocalista Oliver Sykes o parabenizou ao final da música, em show no Rock in Rio: 'Última coisa que ouvi foi o ‘muito bom’ que ele soltou para mim'.
articles.summary: Ao g1, João Pedro Rodrigues, de anos 24, conta que o vocalista Oliver Sykes o parabenizou ao final da música, em show no Rock in Rio: 'Última coisa que ouvi foi o ‘muito bom’ que ele soltou para mim'.
articles.body:
Fã que cantou com Bring me the Horizon diz que estava 'preparado para ser humilhado na internet' — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram

João Pedro Rodrigues já até mudou o avatar de suas redes sociais após um dia histórico em sua vida. Na nova foto: ele e Oliver Sykes, vocalista do Bring me the Horizon, cantando juntos.

No sábado (5), o jovem de 24 anos foi o escolhido pela banda inglesa para subir ao palco e cantar a música "Pray for Plagues", do álbum "Count Your Blessings". O Bring me the Horizon se apresentou no Palco Mundo, no Rock in Rio.

Ao g1 , ele contou que assistia ao show bem perto da grade quando foi convocado. E apesar de já ter um vídeo postado nas redes cantando essa música, ficou surpreso com a escolha de Oli para a apresentação.

"É uma música bem difícil e que estava ouvindo demais desde que eles regravaram o primeiro álbum. Estava tentando aprender ela, já tinha até um vídeo postado no meu TikTok cantando ela no karaokê um tempo atrás. Mas naquela época, eu ainda achava que ele iria chamar para cantar ‘Antivist’, do ‘Sempiternal’, que também tenho na ponta da língua."

João não é música, mas já teve algumas bandas covers em seu tempo de escola, só que os projetos não foram para frente. "Quem sabe agora não rola depois dessa chance com o Oli, né?"

Ele ainda diz que ficou feliz e surpreso com os elogios do público com seu gutural, uma técnica de distorção vocal muito usada por artistas do metal para emitir sons graves e "rasgados".

"Pô, eu realmente queria que tivesse saído melhor, mas do jeito que eu tava no palco, quase morrendo, acho que foi o melhor que deu", brinca.

"Mas fiquei feliz demais com os elogios. Já estava preparado pra ser humilhado na Internet quando saí, mesmo tendo realizado um sonho."

"Mas com todos os elogios que recebi e continuo recebendo, o pessoal achando que foi combinado, a experiência de ter cantado com o Oliver foi mais foda ainda."

João diz que não teve mais contato com a banda depois de descer do palco, mas ficou marcado por um elogio do próprio Oli ao final da apresentação.

"Estava torcendo para que eu pudesse falar com a banda depois do show, mas só pude abraçá-lo e dar um oi antes de entrar no palco. E a última coisa que ouvi foi o ‘Muito bom’ que o Oli soltou para mim no fim da música. Fiquei feliz demais pelo reconhecimento dele. Inacreditável."

articles.title: She won Hollywood's highest honor. So why was making her next film so hard?
articles.summary: Five years after her Oscar-winning 'CODA,' filmmaker Siân Heder talks about 'Being Heumann,' her new movie opening Toronto, and how her life changed.
articles.body:
It's pronounced "human." Yet writer-director Siân Heder acknowledges that the unusual spelling of the title of her new movie, "Being Heumann," is something people might give a puzzled second look, unsure of how to say it and possibly dismissing it altogether.

Which, the more she sat with it, made it perfect as the title for a portrait of real-life disability rights activist Judy Heumann , who, while being in a wheelchair, made herself undismissable.

More specifically, the film looks at the pivotal 1977 protest in which Heumann led a group in a 26-day sit-in at a federal office building in San Francisco until the government began enforcing Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 — the first federal law that recognized disability as a civil rights category.

"The fact that her last name was 'human' has so many beautiful layers of meaning," says Heder, 49, during a recent interview in Los Angeles. "I think Judy was asking for the world to see disabled people as human beings who were worthy of rights and being looked at and being included."

A world premiere and the opening-night selection of this year's Toronto International Film Festival, which begins on Thursday, "Being Heumann" will hit theaters Nov. 6 and begin streaming on Apple TV Nov. 13. It is also, crucially, Heder's first film since 2021's "CODA," the bittersweet drama about a young woman in a Deaf family (the title is an acronym for "child of Deaf adults") that won three Academy Awards including adapted screenplay for Heder and best picture.

In Heumann, a wheelchair user after contracting polio as a child, Heder found a subject who was in the process of discovering herself as a leader: learning when to hold firm and when to cede ground and empower other people. And for someone who was grappling with the aftermath of unexpected success, that felt familiar.

"I think I was making a movie about myself, honestly," Heder says. "When you're moving forward on a massive project or a movement or anything, there's a necessary drive and ambition and focus that is needed. And if you look at any major change that's happened in human history, it takes a certain kind of person to push that through. I'm not identifying myself with great leaders of the civil rights movement, but directing a movie is a similar thing."

Heder is tucked into a quiet corner of a busy coffee shop in L.A.'s Eagle Rock neighborhood, where she has long lived. She is in the process of moving from one historic house to an even older one a few blocks away. Heder didn't want to disrupt the schooling of her two young children, ages 10 and 12, and has become too enmeshed in the area to want to leave it.

Community is a word that comes up often over the course of a conversation with Heder, who has a warm manner and a quiet self-possession. Though "CODA" may have brought her wider attention, she was far from a novice by the time she made that film. She won a Peabody Award as a writer on the series "Men of a Certain Age" and was a writer, director and producer on the acclaimed "Orange Is the New Black." She expanded her 2006 short film "Mother" into her first feature "Tallulah," about a young woman who takes a baby from a reckless mother and tries to pass it off as her own. It premiered at Sundance in 2016.

Winning the Oscar created changes in her life both big and small. Heder at first kept it on her desk at home, but had to move it because she began to feel the statuette's crossed arms quietly judging her as she worked. When she drove herself to the Spirit Awards the year after "CODA's" triumph and spontaneously gave a ride to an afterparty to Maggie Gyllenhaal and Ebon Moss-Bachrach, Heder suddenly realized her 10-year-old Subaru wasn't going to cut it anymore.

"I have a nicer car now," she says, laughing at the memory. "It's baby steps."

The day after the Oscars, Heder recalls that she couldn't stop crying, all the pressure built up from months of campaigning events and Q&As finally letting itself out.

She says two things changed almost immediately after winning the Oscar. One was a sense of expectation, wanting to make the most of whatever the moment might allow.

"This was not a part of my plans," she says. "I didn't ever intend to have so many eyeballs turn to me and go, 'What are you doing now?'"

The second was simply the volume of material and opportunities incoming. Heder says she met with Marvel "so many times" about different projects but none of them felt right. As an independent filmmaker "you're always pushing against the no," she puts it, moving projects forward against all odds. But now she felt she had to be the resistance, the one to ask whether something was worthwhile.

"Suddenly there are a lot of voices chiming in too because your reps have an idea of what you should do next and the industry has an idea of what you should do next," Heder says. "And it was really important for me to center myself back in a feeling of: I've always been drawn to stories because they move me . And that hasn't changed."

Her Oscars triumph was also the night of the notorious Will Smith-Chris Rock on-stage slap , which overshadowed coverage. Heder is online enough that she knows that some film fans would want an asterisk next to the Oscar wins for "CODA," as if to note some sort of COVID-era exception for the first film from a streaming service to win Hollywood's top award.

"There's definitely an element of: 'She manipulated everyone with that movie. She made us all cry and that's why she won,'" Heder says with a edge of defiance. "I was an indie filmmaker that was compelled to tell that story. And then audiences embraced that story and that story took off in a way that was unexpected and surprising even for me."

Heder had been developing "Being Heumann" before "CODA" was released. A friend encouraged Heder to see the 2020 documentary "Crip Camp," which includes Heumann as a subject, and the filmmaker was so struck by that story, she followed up by reading Heumann's 2020 memoir.

She sent Heumann a cold email expressing interest in the book. As it turned out, Heumann was deciding that very day who should direct a movie of her life. Heumann gave the filmmaker a last-minute chance to pitch herself. After saying she'd cast authentically disabled performers as she did on "CODA," Heder got the job.

Heder would work for two years on researching and developing the project with Heumann, interviewing dozens of people involved in the actual Carter-era protest. When Heumann died unexpectedly in 2023, Heder did not think she could continue, but it was "Crip Camp" co-director James LeBrecht who convinced her otherwise.

"I think Judy's death, which was sudden — it made me feel like she had left her legacy in my hands," remembers Heder.

After developing other scripts post-Oscars that never quite became her next film, Heder eventually found herself in the enviable position of having two projects greenlit at once: "Being Heumann" at Apple and an adaptation of Gabrielle Zevin's popular novel "Tomorrow and Tomorrow and Tomorrow" at Paramount.

As she was trying to make a decision, she went to a meeting with several other directors about the relaunching of the Village Theater in Westwood. She found herself having coffee with Guillermo del Toro and asked him how he decided between potential projects.

"And he said, 'Make the movie that can't get made without you,'" she recalls. "And that was very clarifying for me. When you are the element that gets that story told, it takes on an importance and urgency."

As can often be the case, Del Toro's advice confirmed what she already felt and she began to move forward with "Being Heumann." (She is currently prepping "Tomorrow and Tomorrow and Tomorrow" so there will not be another five-year gap between releasing films.)

"I was having a rare moment of power in the industry to push something forward," Heder says, "and it felt like there was a path to go make a big paycheck and have that kind of jump up, or I could use that moment of power and success to try to push through the hardest project I could think of. It was in that moment, after 'CODA,' where I really realized: I could make this incredibly difficult movie that no one might make."

Following what Heder describes as "the casting Olympics,' she arrived at BAFTA-nominated actor Ruth Madeley, a wheelchair user, to play the lead role. "Being Heumann" was shot in Toronto, largely on a soundstage built to stand in for the San Francisco federal office building where the sit-in took place.

"Hollywood might be the least accessible industry out there," Heder notes while beginning to explain the accommodations that needed to be made for a cast that included performers with a wide range of disabilities. Custom-built trailers were created and the set had to be made accessible in ways that a filming location typically is not. An accessibility team oversaw everything, from large-scale logistics to the personal needs of individual background actors.

Rather than a more conventional biopic, Heder wanted to tell the more specific story of the 504 sit-in, building out an ensemble of characters around Heumann.

"I said, "It's almost like 'Bad News Bears' and 'Dog Day Afternoon' together," says Heder. "There's an underdog-sports-team feeling and bank-heist-gone-wrong."

But a filmmaker friend asked her: Is making movies about disability now her "thing"? It is a question Heder had already considered.

"Of course it was on my mind if it starts to feel like: Oh, is Siân Heder a social justice warrior who's just out to try to make these movies that have some kind of message behind them," she says preemptively. "But I think this is just a great story. Outside of disability, outside of anything else, it is a great story."

Heder remains interested in stories about outsiders, about class and people generally ignored by or on the fringes of society. And it remains important that she herself feel a part of a larger community in her life and her work.

"My daughter said to me the other day, 'Mom, I think you're the right kind of famous because you are important to people who know who you are, but you can still just be in the world and be anonymous." And I think there's something true about that."

Her daughter has obviously inherited Heder's deep well of empathy, one that is more concerned with bringing new, unseen stories to the screen than with the pursuit of cool points or pure fame.

"'Earnest' has become a dirty word," says Heder. "And what earnest actually means is direct and truthful."

This story originally appeared in Los Angeles Times .

articles.title: Selena Gomez Sells Encino Mansion for $5.4 Million—After Snapping Up $35 Million Marital Home
articles.summary: The 34-year-old singer and actress purchased the six-bedroom, 8.5-bathroom dwelling for $4.89 million in 2020
articles.body:
Pop icon Selena Gomez has officially offloaded her sprawling Encino abode in Los Angeles for $5.399 million—four months after listing the property and shortly after picking up a $35 million marital mansion.

The 34-year-old singer and actress purchased the six-bedroom, 8.5-bathroom dwelling for $4.89 million in 2020, around three years before she began dating Benny Blanco , 38, whom she wed in September 2025.

However, after she and her husband snapped up a new, much larger Beverly Hills dwelling for $35 million in February 2025, it seemed Gomez no longer needed her former bachelorette pad, which spans nearly 11,500 square feet and sits on just under an acre.

Gomez's ownership of the dwelling was mentioned in the listing—which also noted that the property was formerly home to another music legend, Tom Petty , who had the home custom built in 1989 and owned it until 2017, when it was sold just a few months before his death.

Before Gomez purchased the property six years ago, it underwent a meticulous renovation and is now described as a "private celebrity compound" that "evokes a magical vision of romance, inspiration, and tranquility."

"Formerly home to music icon Tom Petty and superstar Selena Gomez, this spectacular estate offers distinctive architecture crafted with exceptional attention to detail and the finest quality," the listing added.

The five-bedroom mansion with soaring ceilings and a gourmet kitchen features a rockin' lower level that includes a wine cellar, gym, massage room, creative work area, kitchen, vocal booth, den, and guest suite.

Upon entering the home, guests are greeted with an expansive living area that features a chic fireplace.

"The front entry opens to the living room, immediately setting the stage with sophisticated architecture and soaring ceilings. The home includes a family room, formal dining room, and a sprawling kitchen," the listing read.

On the main level, there is the gorgeous primary suit, which comes complete with a wooden ceiling and enough space for a king-sized bed.

"The main level features a spectacular primary suite, complemented by an upper-level second primary suite and four additional bedroom suites," added the listing.

The kitchen is certainly the crown jewel of the home thanks to its marble countertops, island, and brick stove.

The primary bathroom features a dual vanity, a glass-enclosed shower, and a large soaking tub.

Heading to the lower level, guests will see a wine cellar, gym, massage room, office, glam room, a kitchen, and a vocal booth, which is thought to have been part of Petty's original recording studio—and will likely have served as the perfect place for Gomez to write her latest hits.

Gomez's personal touches are still visible in several rooms of the house, although listing images show that it has been completely cleared of all her personal belongings, including a fun floral wallpaper that has been added to an area of the glam room.

There is also a sizable home movie theater that, in a not-so-subtle nod to the property's celebrity owner, was photographed with a video of Gomez performing flashed up on the screen.

Outside the property is just as luxurious, with numerous entertaining areas spread around the grounds, as well as a stunning swimming pool and spa that provides the perfect place to relax.

"The idyllic exterior grounds include a cabana with bar, fire pit, al fresco dining area, and a cascading waterfall and stream flowing into the pool and spa. Here is your chance to live amongst the stars," the listing read.

While the home served as Gomez's primary residence for several years, she and her husband have since moved on to an even splashier dwelling.

Gomez and Blanco splashed out on an enormous $35 million marital abode in Beverly Hills in December 2024—the very same week they got engaged.

They shared their exciting relationship update on Dec. 11, when the actress shared a series of images of herself modeling a dazzling diamond on that finger, revealing that her beau popped the question while they were enjoying a Taco Bell picnic.

However, what she didn't reveal at the time was that she and Blanco had just closed on a stunning seven-bedroom, 12-bathroom dwelling, which they purchased on Dec. 4, according to records seen by Realtor.com ® .

The property actually comprises two lots that are home to an expansive main residence and two separate guesthouses—one of which boasts its own studio, while the other houses a home theater.

Prior to being purchased by Gomez and Blanco, the property was owned by a famous Hollywood director, according to TMZ , which first reported the news of the sale.

When the singer and her fiancé bought the home, it marked one of the priciest sales in the area in 2024.

The Spanish-inspired, opulent pad features a spiral staircase and library. Outside the mansion, there is a fitness center, pool, and a glass greenhouse solarium, which is a nod to Blanco's green thumb; the singer has been known to use his garden to give back to the community.

The property is surrounded by lush landscaping and features sophisticated stone flooring encompassing the pool.

Gomez and Blanco purchased the property in an off-market deal that was carried out via an LLC that is associated with the music producer's business manager.

The property was last sold in August 2021, when it was picked up for $30.7 million.

At the time, it was described in its listing as a "true masterwork" and a "perfect combination of authentic details, fine craftsmanship, and the best modern amenities."

The listing noted that the home featured an array of different living spaces, including a "fairytale playroom" and a "sensational living room."

Gomez recently shared a glimpse inside the couple's martial home, revealing that they have focused on incorporating color into the property with vibrant shelves and blue cabinets in their kitchen.

She also shared a photo of the backyard, revealing that it comes complete with lush greenery and a rose-covered patio.

articles.title: Skillet's John Cooper says woke activists have 'big hearts' but are 'hurting themselves'
articles.summary: Skillet musician John Cooper gets candid about about how wokeness can harm people and explains why he doesn't believe in cancel culture.
articles.body: Skillet frontman John Cooper believes people labeled "woke" are often motivated by good intentions — but warned their approach can ultimately "hurt society." "I think it’s really worth mentioning that people that we would call woke, the things that we find really problematic, I think it's worth mentioning that most of those people really have big hearts," Cooper said during a recent appearance on the "Unashamed with the Robertson Family" podcast. "They want justice. They want the world to be better." "They’re just going about it in a way that they don’t know is wrong, and it’s actually hurting them," he continued. "It’s hurting everybody. It hurts society." SKILLET’S JOHN COOPER SAYS CHRISTIANS WHO CALL ROCK MUSIC ‘DEMONIC’ ARE ‘GETTING THE GOSPEL WRONG’ He said that inner cities in particular are "getting so much worse," saying, "I look at the things that the politicians that say they want to help the poor, they want to help the marginalized, they want to help people of color, whatever it may be, and all they do is keep hurting them more and more and more." BRANTLEY GILBERT SLAMS ARTISTS WHO BACK OUT OF PATRIOTIC SHOWS UNDER HEAT Cooper said he believes that "the woke probably have good intentions," and pointed to people he knows personally as proof. "I know these people. Some of them work for me. They’ve worked for me for 15 years. I love them," he said. "And I say to them, ‘I know you’re trying to be a good person, but it’s going to hurt people.’" The musician ultimately attributed his disagreement with those views to his Christian faith. "What they’re doing is not true, and it’s not based on the Bible," Cooper said. "It goes against the way God tells us how to live. They end up hurting themselves, and now we've got a culture so nihilistic that doesn't know that they matter. They're looking to matter by doing social justice, but they keep hurting themselves more." GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE Cooper, who has been performing with Skillet for roughly 30 years, recently told Fox News Digital that his Christian beliefs have influenced some of his professional decisions. However, he remains a steadfast supporter of artistic freedom. "I am a huge believer in freedom of speech," Cooper said. "I hate cancel culture. I don’t want anybody to be canceled because I’ve never said, ‘So-and-so rock artist sings a song against Jesus and I want him pulled down from Spotify.’" "I would never say that, because that’s not what art is," he added. Cooper said he has shared the stage with artists who are atheists and even those who openly oppose Christianity. "Some of them, I would say, are probably personally not only atheist, they probably personally are a little anti-Christ," he said. "And they would know it. They would say, ‘The truth is, John, I just hate the concept of Jesus.’ And we’re still friends." LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? "I can only think of two things in my entire career I’ve turned down," he said, recalling a band that planned to feature "Jesus on an upside-down cross" during its stage show. "I don’t think I want to tour with that act," Cooper said. "And it’s not because I hate them. I don’t hate them at all. I’m not calling for them to be pulled down from Spotify. I just go, ‘Hey, this is just something that you’ve gone a little too far to desecrate something that I think is sacred.’" PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE Cooper said he believes people with opposing viewpoints should be free to express themselves. "I would like to share my faith in Jesus," he said. "And because of that, I don’t mind if somebody else sings a song that’s against what I believe. Freedom of speech. articles.title: ‘Double Lives of Suburban Wives’ star went from food stamps to making $100K a month
articles.summary: From food stamps and a $200 grocery budget to $100K months, Emily Smith's journey on TLC's "Double Lives of Suburban Wives" defies all expectations.
articles.body: Emily Smith’s life has gone from scraping together grocery money to bringing home six figures in a single month. The 37-year-old stay-at-home mom of four, featured on TLC’s "Double Lives of Suburban Wives," said her family once relied on food stamps, struggled with housing and had just $200 to spend on groceries for six people. Now, she said her adult-content business generated more than $1 million last year. 'DOUBLE LIVES OF SUBURBAN WIVES' STAR SAYS SECRET ADULT-CONTENT SIDE HUSTLE GOT HER FIRED FROM CORPORATE JOB And the suburban mom said the moment it finally sank in that her family’s financial life had changed came after one particularly massive month. "I think staying in the 100K a month that's the moment we were like, ‘Well, holy moly,’" Smith told Fox News Digital. "Who would’ve ever expected something like that to happen? Not us, for sure." But getting there was anything but an overnight success. The adult-content creation business, she explained, is notoriously unpredictable. It tapers down, it tapers down and then — this world of content creating is very roller-coaster-y," Smith said. Eventually, one month refused to taper off. "There was a month that really, really hit, and then it never went down and hasn't gone down, and we're like, ‘Oh, oh my God,;" she said. 'KNOTS LANDING' STAR DONNA MILLS SAYS REFUSING TO POSE NUDE COST HER PLAYBOY COVER Smith’s story is at the center of TLC’s new reality series, "Double Lives of Suburban Wives," which takes viewers behind the polished façades of suburban lifestyle — and into the unconventional careers happening behind closed doors. That second life comes with some unexpected and bizarre requests. One of Smith’s strangest adult-content requests came with a $2,000 price tag and an unusual ask — she was paid to "lay an egg." "So that request was $2,000," she said. Smith's niche includes what she describes as "kinky weird adult content," with requests involving wedgies, fart content and "giant" videos — a fetish centered on fantasies of giants. "I love to make people’s fantasies come true — if I can do it, I will do it," she said. WATCH: ‘DOUBLE LIVES OF SUBURBAN WIVES’ STAR’S ADULT CONTENT BOOM PUSHES HUSBAND OUT OF 9-TO-5 The "giant" videos hold a particular appeal for Smith, who is just 5 feet, 1 inch tall. Joining the group is about more than money, the reality star said. She is also looking for people who understand a life that can be difficult to explain to outsiders. Back at home, however, Smith looks like the quintessential suburban mom. She cooks, cleans and cuts her children’s hair. The family eats dinner together every night. WATCH: 'DOUBLE LIVES OF SUBURBAN WIVES' STAR SAYS $100 LINGERIE VIDEO SPARKED NEW CAREER The Smiths share four children — sons ages 17, 15 and 12, and an 8-year-old daughter — along with six cats and a dog. Her husband, Nathan, eventually quit his 9-to-5 job to help her keep up with the business. He had been a store manager for a pharmaceutical company. articles.title: Sandra Bullock's wake-up call that changed everything during late partner Bryan Randall’s illness
articles.summary: Sandra Bullock reveals her sister's urgent warning forced her to confront the hidden toll of caregiving during partner Bryan Randall's private ALS battle.
articles.body: A sobering warning from Sandra Bullock’s sister became a wake-up call for the actress as she quietly navigated her late partner Bryan Randall’s battle with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS). Bullock reflected on how caring for Randall through his illness forced her to recognize her own limits – and ultimately ask for help after years of putting others first. "I'm always a caretaker," she said during an appearance on "Good Hang with Amy Poehler." "Always. And I learned that I didn't take care of the person that was taking care of everybody else. articles.body: El creador de contenido gastronómico Alfonso Ortega, conocido como 'CociTuber', ha denunciado públicamente y ante la Guardia Civil una agresión física sufrida en Comillas, Cantabria. El ataque se produjo cuando un hostelero le abordó por la espalda y le propinó un puñetazo motivado por una reseña negativa publicada hace más de dos años. Aunque ya explicó lo sucedido en sus redes sociales, el influencer ha visitado este miércoles 9 de septiembre, el programa ‘Espejo Público’ para profundizar más en el asunto. "Una cosa es ser mal hostelero y otra es ser un malnacido. Suelo hacer un artículo periodístico y luego, en mis historias, cuento un poco sobre la gastronomía, restaurantes y el tipo de comida", comenzaba diciendo. A continuación, CociTuber ha contado cómo se produjo la agresión: “Era un hombre enormísimo, me agarró del cuello con todas sus fuerzas, me pegó un puñetazo en la espalda y me tiró al suelo. Como soy influencer, pues empecé a grabar”, detallaba. “Fui a hacer una crítica y no creo que sea nada malo. Siempre intento ir a favor de los restaurantes”, añadía. El creador de contenido gastronómico ha comentado que ha hecho la denuncia por “miedo”: “Un tío de esa envergadura me agarra y puede matarme”, afirmaba, asegurando que varios camareros del local salieron a increparle. Finalmente, la abogada Beatriz de Vicente ha apuntado: "Le condenan seguro". Hay que destacar que Alfonso Ortega, o 'Cocituber', es uno de los influencers y creadores de contenido gastronómico más populares de España. Cuenta con más de un millón de seguidores sumando sus diferentes redes sociales y su enfoque suele estar centrado en ‘comida de barrio’. Aunque en los últimos su contenido se ha diversificado más al acudir a grandes restaurantes.

Angelina Jolie is ready for a new chapter overseas following the end of her custody agreement with ex-husband Brad Pitt . In a rare new interview published on September 9, the Maleficent actress detailed her plans to leave her life in the U.S. behind—as well as what she'll be doing once she's living abroad.

Jolie opened up to L'Officiel about her plans to move away from Los Angeles, the city where she was born and has raised her six children: Maddox, 24 ; Pax, 22 ; Zahara, 21; Shiloh, 20; and twins Knox and Vivienne, 18. The Mr. and Mrs. Smith star—who previously revealed she was unable to leave L.A. until her kids turned 18 — has already begun making inroads into this future, recently listing her Los Feliz estate on the market for $29.85 million in May.

"It's the end of a certain time for me," Jolie told the publication about her new beginnings. And while the 51-year-old star is ready to leave L.A. behind, she's not quite ready to put down roots. As her first order of business, the Eternals actress is focused on growing her brand Atelier Jolie "out of the States more" after launching its flagship in New York City.

"The hope for the Atelier was always to be global; Brazil might become the first space that we open outside of the U.S.," she explained. "The idea would be to visit the different locations around the world and meet local artists and makers." Jolie said she'll also be continuing with her humanitarian work, adding, "I'm going to get back to doing more hands-on work with my foundation in Cambodia and my field work."

However, Jolie clarified that she's embracing the freedom of this new era, saying she doesn't "really plan to have a base." She shared, "I'd like to have a home base for my family, a place where some of the mom stuff and the family photos are. And then I'd like to be a bit nomadic for a while. My home in Cambodia will also be a residency a few months out of the year for Khmer culture."

articles.title: Charles Reportedly Bracing for ‘All-Out War’ with ‘Unleashed’ Harry & Meghan—They’re ‘No Longer Afraid of the Consequences’
articles.summary: What did they do now?
articles.body:
Prince Harry and Meghan Markle have adopted a strategy of publicly challenging Palace statements, believing silence failed them before, and are no longer afraid of the consequences.

Prince William is reportedly "absolutely fuming" and suspects that Harry and Meghan think they will be accepted back onto the Royal roster, potentially leading to an "all-out war" within the royal family.

Prince Charles was reportedly less than happy to learn that British security officials were informed about Harry's return before he was, leading to further strain in their relationship as the King seeks advice on minimizing risk to the family.

Ever since Prince Harry and Meghan Markle touched down in the UK, everyone has been speculating about what their return means, not just for their relationships with the British royal family, but for their role as royals. Will they return to the fold? Will they remain private citizens, just in the UK? Can the family really find peace at least?

According to Hollywood insider Rob Shuter , that's still up in the air, particularly because the Duke and Duchess of Sussex seemed to have adopted a strategy of publicly challenging Palace statements, according to the gossip journalist.

"Harry and Meghan feel completely unleashed," a royal source told Shuter's Naughty But Nice . "They believe silence failed them before, so now their attitude is: if the Palace says something they don't like, they will answer. They're no longer afraid of the consequences."

How will the King respond? "Charles will not turn the monarchy into a reality show," the source said. "He isn't going to respond to every complaint, accusation or perceived slight. The Crown has survived far bigger storms by refusing to wrestle in the mud."

Prince William , however, might be another matter altogether. And it could reportedly turn into an "all-out war."

"They're absolutely fuming to be blindsided like this but, like the King, there's nothing they can do about it," a source told Woman's Day about William and Kate Middleton 's reaction to Harry and Meghan's return to the UK.

"William suspects Harry and Meghan actually do think they're going to be accepted back onto the Royal roster," the insider continued. "It may not happen overnight, but William's convinced this is their long game – and he's stunned that Harry thinks there would be even remotely a chance."

Reportedly, the heir to the throne has been participating in "intense meetings on how to minimise any risk to him and the family. He'll be seeking advice from everyone from lawyers to diplomatic-crisis experts."

Sounds a little dramatic. But this is the royal family. Plus, reports say Charles was less than happy to learn that his son allegedly told British security officials about his return before he was told.

"The King understands perfectly well why the appropriate authorities needed advance warning, particularly given Harry's long-running concerns about security," a royal source told RadarOnline . "What angered him and made him furious was discovering that officials apparently knew something as significant as his son's return before he did."

The insider added that, "after everything that has happened between them, Charles regarded that as extremely disappointing. This isn't some routine visit lasting a couple of days – Harry is bringing his wife and children back to Britain."

And it's on the list of things that might affect their relationship. "The King wants a relationship with his son and particularly wants opportunities to see his grandchildren. Against that background, finding himself further down the information chain than the Home Office was never going to improve matters."

articles.title: John Malkovich cancels Tel Aviv show after promoter fabricates statement from him on Israel
articles.summary: John Malkovich cancelled a show in Tel Aviv after learning The Jerusalem Post unknowingly published a made-up a quote about his “solidarity” with Israeli audiences.
articles.body: Oscar-nominated actor John Malkovich cancelled an upcoming stage performance in Tel Aviv after learning that The Jerusalem Post unknowingly published a made-up a quote attributed to him about his “closeness and solidarity” with Israeli audiences. Malkovich, in a statement to The Hollywood Reporter on Tuesday, said a local public relations firm “hired by the Israeli promoter drafted a quote for the article that was attributed to me, though I never made the statements that were quoted, nor was I consulted before they were printed.” “The fact that they were printed as direct quotes from me is unacceptable and untenable,” his statement read. “For this reason, I have decided I cannot participate in the Tel Aviv performance.” The offending quote, which NBC News obtained by using The Wayback Machine internet archive, was published by The Jerusalem Post on Saturday. It said: “I am thrilled to return to Israel and look forward to meeting the warm Israeli audience once again, to whom I feel a strong closeness and solidarity. I hope to find you happy and optimistic! Sending you much love.” After Malkovich complained, the newspaper updated its story to include an apology from the show’s Israeli producer, Alon Yurik. “I would like to clarify that the original press release contained a mistake, and an incorrect quote from Malkovich was included due to a misunderstanding,” Yurik stated. “I would like to take this opportunity to apologize for that.” It also included a slightly different version of the offending quote attributed to Malkovich: “I am excited to return to Israel and would be very happy to meet again with the warm Israeli audience, with whom I feel great closeness and identification.” Tal Spungin, the newspaper’s managing editor, said in an email to NBC News that the “difference is due to a discrepancy in the translation of the quote.” “It was initially provided to our Hebrew-language sister publication, Walla, in Hebrew, and was then translated into English for The Jerusalem Post,” Spungin wrote. “The quote was removed from our report after the production company confirmed to us that it was fabricated, and the wording was amended in our follow-up to better reflect the nature of the ‘quote’ as it was provided in Hebrew.” Malkovich, 72, is the latest high-profile artist who had declined to perform in Israel amid the ongoing conflicts with Palestinians in Gaza and the West Bank. But he did not directly criticize Israel. Instead, in his statement, Malkovich said he counted himself as “lucky” to have had the opportunity to perform “in countries with governments whose values or culture I do not share” and the chance to travel to places “whose view of the world may not align with mine.” “My appearance in any country, even my own, does not constitute approval of said country’s policies, nor actions, nor its elected or unelected leaders,” his statement said. “My appearances would also not condone nor mean that I am in supposed ‘solidarity’ with any particular political cause, nor with the killing of innocents, nor with any acts of terrorism, nor any other kind of barbarity.” Representatives for Malkovich did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Best known for his riveting roles in movies like “Dangerous Liaisons,” “In the Line of Fire” and playing himself in the surreal meta-comedy “Being John Malkovich,” he was supposed to perform “The Music Critic,” a touring comedy featuring classical music and criticism of world-famous composers, next April in Tel Aviv. Malkovich had previously visited Israel in July 2008 as an honorary guest of the Jerusalem Film Festival. In April 2013, Malkovich returned to Israel with his musical theater show The Infernal Comedy: Confessions of a Serial Killer.

articles.title: Sharon Stone says she 'nearly died' after 'Basic Instinct' opened the door to Hollywood's dark side

articles.title: Henry Winkler Addresses Ongoing Tension with Tom Hanks: ‘I Am Still Working on My Perspective’
articles.summary: Hanks guest-starred on ‘Happy Days’ before his movie career took off, while Winkler starred as Fonzie
articles.body:
Henry Winkler is opening up about his relationship with Tom Hanks

Hanks guest-starred on Happy Days before his movie career took off, while Winkler starred as Fonzie

Winkler still owns a signed model plane Hanks built during their time working on Turner & Hooch

Henry Winkler is reflecting on decades-long tension between him and Tom Hanks — and mulling over whether the relationship can be repaired.

In a new interview on In Depth With Graham Bensinger , Winkler touched on being fired as the director of the 1989 film Turner & Hooch , which starred Hanks, now 70.

Winkler said he had a feeling he wasn't "suited" to direct the film, but was hand-picked by a Paramount executive.

"I went completely against my tummy, and it hit me in the face with a 2x4," he said. "I now meet the puppies, and I meet with Tom [Hanks]... and I, at that time being insecure, I talked too much and I gave them direction. I [did] what I thought was my job, and I wanted to do it over again and apparently that pissed them off."

Winkler added: "And in 13 days of filming, I'm called into [studio executive Jeffrey Katzenberg's] office and he said,'It's not in the dailies.' I then go to the set. I get my things. I drive home. I'm fired as a director... I don't handle it well. I'm devastated."

Winkler played breakout star Arthur "Fonzie" Fonzarelli on Happy Days , which ran from 1974 to 1984 and also starred Ron Howard (a frequent collaborator of Hanks') as Richie Cunningham. The series followed the group of friends (plus Richie's family) living in the Midwest in the 1950s and 1960s.

The show also featured Hanks as a guest star, with Winkler noting that on the podcast.

"I don't know because, when Tom, before he was a movie star… he was a guest star on Happy Days . And I don't know," he said. "We did a retrospective of Happy Days , and we wanted 60 seconds of Tom Hanks in his episode and we did not get permission for that."

When asked what his "perspective" on the relationship with Hanks was, Winkler responded, "I am still working on my perspective," adding: "I think his wife, Rita [Wilson], was also a guest on Happy Days in the beginning."

Asked if he thought the relationship would ever "repair itself," Winkler responded, "Sure."

Winkler went on to say he still owns a signed model plane Hanks built for him while working together on Turner & Hooch , before Winkler was fired as director of the film.

"It was a model plane… While we were having meetings he built a plastic Piper Cub or something like that. Yeah," Winkler said.

Winkler starred on Happy Days until the series ended, receiving four Emmy nominations for his time on the show. He won an Emmy in 2018 for his role on Barry as Gene Cousineau, an acting coach .

Hanks, meanwhile, went on from his guest star stint on Happy Days to starring in the sitcom Bosom Buddies. His career eventually transitioned to film, with the actor winning two Academy Awards for acting and carving out a resume that includes roles in such acclaimed films as Forrest Gump, Saving Private Ryan and Philadelphia.

articles.title: Michelle Jenner vuelve a dar plantón a Broncano: “Yo ya sabes que no, prefiero mantener el misterio”
articles.standfirst: La actriz ha sido la nueva invitada de ‘La Revuelta’, de La 1 de RTVE
articles.summary: La actriz ha sido la nueva invitada de ‘La Revuelta’, de La 1 de RTVE
articles.body: Este miércoles, 9 de septiembre, ‘La Revuelta’ ha emitido su tercera entrega de esta nueva temporada en la franja horaria del ‘access prime time’ de La 1 de RTVE. Tras invitados de nivel como Ernesto Sevilla, Joaquín Reyes, Borja Iglesias y Carmen Lomana, el espacio de la cadena pública quiere seguir apostando por rostros potentes con el objetivo de tener un arranque con fuerza. En esta ocasión, una de las invitadas que ha pasado por el Teatro Albeniz de Madrid ha sido una de las actrices más reconocidas de este país, Michelle Jenner, quien ha venido a hablar sobre su nueva película, ‘El nido’, un thriller psicológico que protagoniza junto a Luisa Gavasa y que llegará a los cines este viernes 11 de septiembre. Además, RTVE ha participado en esta película. La intérprete es una vieja amiga del programa, ya que son varias las ocasiones en las que se ha sentado junto a Broncano. Tanto en su etapa en Movistar Plus como en la corporación pública. Una de las preguntas curiosas que le ha hecho el presentador es cuánto es el máximo tiempo que ha pasado sin ducharse. La invitada ha dicho que nunca ha pasado más de un día sin ducharse. “Yo alguna vez he hecho lo típico de que hoy no me lavo el pelo, pero lo importante sí”, confesaba. En ese momento, el comunicador jienense ha apuntado que cuando se iba a la montaña en verano se ha llegado a tirar dos meses sin ducharse. “Llevábamos una especie de toallitas gordas para lo mínimo. A la segunda semana ya estabas acostumbrado”, decía entre risas. Finalmente, en las preguntas clásicas, Michelle Jenner ha vuelto a dar plantón a David Broncano y no ha querido responder: “Yo ya sabes que no, prefiero mantener el misterio”, sentenciaba.

articles.title: Paula Echeverría revela cuáles son sus pros y contras en ‘El Hormiguero’: “Tomo vinos hasta tarde, pero también soy la primera en ir al gimnasio”
articles.standfirst: La intérprete fue la tercera protagonista de la semana en programa de Pablo Motos en Antena 3
articles.summary: La intérprete fue la tercera protagonista de la semana en programa de Pablo Motos en Antena 3
articles.body: ‘El Hormiguero’ emitió la tercera entrega de la vigesimoprimera temporada en Antena 3 este miércoles, 9 de septiembre, con Pablo Motos al frente en Antena 3. La invitada de esta jornada en pleno horario ‘prime time’ fue Paula Echevarría, reconocida actriz de nuestro país que acudió al citado espacio para hablar de ‘A la deriva’, serie en la que encarna a Lucía en Atresplayer y que verá la luz el próximo domingo, 20 de septiembre. Así le dio la bienvenida Motos: “Hoy ha venido a divertirse a nuestro programa Paula Echevarría, que alegría tenerla con nosotros”. “Me encanta volver a estar aquí un año más, pero no vuelvo a grabar más ‘sketch’ promocionales para tus nuevas temporadas porque nunca me sacáis”, añadió Echevarría al respecto, con un mensaje incluido a la producción del espacio de Atresmedia por no sacarla en la promoción de la nueva campaña del programa de Motos, causando las risas del presentador y de todos los presentes en el plató. Posteriormente, llegó el turno de hablar de ‘A la deriva’, momento en el que la actriz contó de qué va a rasgos genéricos: “Una serie amenizada en los años 70 y empieza cuando unos pescadores que dábamos por muertos vuelven después de 2 años y uno de ellos es marido de Lucía, personaje que interpreto, pero yo no quiero que él venga porque he rehecho mi vida”. “La serie está inspirada en una época en la que no eres nada en la vida, ni viuda ni tienes derechos ni nada, hay como un vacío legal. No podías casarte ni sacar dinero sin la firma de tu marido (…) La serie es muy bonita, una superproducción de Atresmedia. Es un drama, pero tiene de todo en un ámbito poco explotado en nuestro país como es en el mar, un serión”, siguió diciendo Paula Echevarría. Luego, Pablo Motos desveló que le habían “chivado” que Echevarría odiaba el pescado y que tenía que manipularlo en la ficción, a lo que añadió la intérprete: “No me gusta nada el olor a pescado y eso que vengo de un pueblo pesquero (Candás, Asturias). Una cosa es ir al supermercado a media mañana y pasar por la pescadería y otra que en la primera secuencia ya tenga que manipular pescado, una vez me corté. Hubo un día que hasta 48 horas después de una secuencia olía a sardina”. El presentador del espacio de Atresmedia le preguntó si tenía una fragancia o remedio para eliminar el olor a pescado, respondiendo la invitada con un tajante “no”. Asimismo, Paula Echevarría contó que Dani Grau, compañero de reparto, durante una secuencia de la mencionada serie, le partió los labios de manera “accidentada”. Además, Echevarría reveló que es la primera en que nada más acaba el rodaje va a tomar algo, sacando a relucir también su pasión por el deporte: “Soy la primera en ir a tomarme unos vinos hasta tarde, pero también soy la primera en ir al gimnasio, es decir, soy fiestera y disciplinada”. Por otro lado, desveló cuál es su rutina de entrenamientos para “verse bien”: “Un poco de glúteo, brazo para que no se caiga y abdomen. Tampoco me mato a entrenar, pero todos los días intento moverme para sentirme bien a nivel mental y en bienestar de salud”. Del mismo modo, comentó que es algo “impuntual”, pero que lo está “corrigiendo bien”: “Todo el mundo está sorprendido por este cambio”. Para finalizar, afirmó que cuando vino por última vez a ‘El Hormiguero’ se puso un flequillo postizo y que sus platos favoritos son los escalopines al cabrales, cachopo, la comida asturiana y la pasta: “Hago la ley del gym y ñam, no voy al gimnasio para competir, voy para comer”.

articles.summary: Mel Gibson revealed why "The Resurrection of the Christ" ditches ancient languages for English and takes viewers on a spiritual journey across realms.
articles.body: Mel Gibson is ditching ancient languages for English in his upcoming two-part follow-up to "The Passion of the Christ," describing the new epic as a "trip" that will take moviegoers across spiritual realms. Gibson spoke exclusively with Fox News contributor Raymond Arroyo about his upcoming two-part follow-up, "The Resurrection of the Christ," including his decision to use English in the new films. The interview comes as the original 2004 film returns to theaters for a special Fathom Events re-release. The full interview is featured on the "Arroyo Grande Show with Raymond Arroyo" YouTube channel. 'RESURRECTION OF THE CHRIST' WRITER REVEALS MEL GIBSON'S DARK SPIRITUAL WARNING ABOUT 'PASSION' FOLLOW-UP "You had a focal point, and it was about human suffering," Gibson said of the original film. "That was a rather simpler message to get across, and I think the complexity of an event like the resurrection, which is impossible to comprehend really, one has to delve more into sources. "I thought it was just silly to make people read subtitles in a foreign language when they were dealing with such heady concepts. So, it asks more of you, but we help them along with their own language." "The Passion of the Christ" is a biblical drama depicting the crucifixion of Jesus Christ in excruciating detail. It starred Jim Caviezel as Jesus and focused on the final 12 hours of Jesus’ life, with dialogue mainly in Aramaic, Hebrew and Latin. MEL GIBSON'S 'RESURRECTION OF THE CHRIST' REVEALS FIRST PHOTOS AFTER LONG-AWAITED PASSION SEQUEL "The Resurrection of the Christ: Part One" is set for release May 6, 2027, with Part Two scheduled for May 25, 2028. While the original film focused on the final hours of Jesus’ life, Gibson said the new films will explore the resurrection and the days that followed. Gibson said the upcoming films take viewers on a "trip" into other realms and explore how humanity is connected to them. He said the films are meant to show viewers the "big picture." "It takes a pretty broad trip [from] our own broken world to, you know, other realms and stuff with different natures, and connects all of them, I hope — because we're all connected, and we all know we're connected," he said. NEW BOOK ON ARCHAEOLOGICAL EVIDENCE FOR JESUS ROCKETS TO TOP OF BESTSELLER LIST Gibson said the writing and pre-production process has taken more than a decade, and the new films are arriving over 20 years after the original premiered. He suggested the timing may be for a reason, saying, "There’s no accidents anywhere." "I thought I was late. It was just too late, 23 years later, but it's probably just right. It's not my timing," Gibson said. When asked whether he considers the project his own "resurrection" as a filmmaker, Gibson described the undertaking as a transformative, communal journey. articles.body: Fans of the 'Game Of Thrones' universe could not believe their eyes when a social media post claimed that Christopher Nolan could direct the first big-screen 'Game of Thrones'.A post that went viral online, claimed that Nolan is being eyed to helm the film titled 'Game of Thrones: Aegon’s Conquest'. While the news sparked buzz among fans to see the director's vision come to life after 'The Odyssey', many others were rather sceptical.The claim was posted online by the X account @Culturecrave, which described itself as a parody account, and stated that Warner Bros. and HBO are "are attempting to convince Christopher Nolan to direct the in-development ‘GAME OF THRONES: AEGON’S CONQUEST’ movie. The studios are prepared to sanction the use of IMAX cameras as part of the pitch.'"However, an official studio announcement, is sill awaited. Nonetheless, fans embraced the possibility of Nolan joining the franchise. Known for his work with practical effects, netizens had a field day laughing at the possibility of the director bringing Westeros alive with his tongue-in-cheek humour. While one suggested that the director will use "real dragons" for the film, others claimed that the director could have just cast his frequent collaborators like Florence Pugh and Anne Hathaway.What is confirmed about the Game of Thrones movie?Warner Bros. confirmed the development of its first 'Game of Thrones' feature film at CinemaCon in April 2026. The project was presented as Game of Thrones: Aegon’s Conquest as part of the studio's “2027 and beyond” slate.The film will focus on Aegon I Targaryen, better known as Aegon the Conqueror, the first Targaryen ruler to unite much of Westeros under a single crown.
